docs.title: Xp-clean
docs.text:
Xp-clean discovers and cleans up Crossplane v2 composition trees — test GVKs and leftover instances left behind in shared clusters.

It targets v2-native stacks only (Namespaced and modern Cluster XRs). LegacyCluster claims are not supported: there is no claim discovery or deletion path.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
1. Discover CompositeResourceDefinitions and build parent→child traces (XR → spec.crossplane.resourceRefs → children; nested XRs supported).
  2. Select eligible stacks with labels and/or glob patterns (AND when both are set). Namespace alone never implies eligibility.
  3. Plan deletions under configurable deletion.scope: instances-only (default) or all.
  4. Execute safely — dry-run by default, budgets, skip paused resources, never strip Crossplane finalizers.
  5. Notify (optional) via Microsoft Teams Workflows on run start / finish / failure.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: Xp-clean is a Go CLI (and future in-cluster controller) for scheduled discovery and cleanup of Crossplane v2-native composition trees.

docs.title: MVP implemented in this repository
docs.text:
• Dynamic XRD discovery + instance trace build (no claims)
  • Eligibility via labels and/or globs + TTL (pkg/match); GVK globs are group/version
  • deletion.scope with default instances-only
  • Boolean dry-run planner + optional deletes; skip paused by default
  • File / labelled ConfigMap policy (multi-tenant); explicit --config for file override
  • Cobra CLI: run / plan / trace / manager / version / completion
  • Layout: thin cmd/xp-clean, internal/cli helpers, domain in pkg/
  • Optional Teams Workflows notification hooks around RunOnce
  • GoReleaser + private GHCR on SemVer tags; CI with golangci-lint

docs.title: Deferred
docs.text: CleanupPolicy CRD + controller-runtime manager, Prometheus exporters, Helm chart, RBAC generator, kubectl plugin alias, multi-cluster, Slack sink implementation, audit retention sinks, SPDX licence packaging.

docs.title: Design plans
docs.text: Longer design notes are maintained alongside the Cursor project for this repository (architecture, release plumbing, notification hooks). Product behaviour summarised in these docs should match those locked decisions; when in doubt, prefer the samples under config/samples/ and the CLI help text in the current release.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text: Standalone Cobra binary xp-clean. kubectl plugin documentation is deferred — use the standalone CLI for now.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
xp-clean run --once [--config PATH] [--policy-namespace NS] [--dry-run=true|false] [--scope instances-only|all] [--fail-on-blocked] [--notify] [--notify-on-dry-run] [--kubeconfig PATH] [--context NAME]
xp-clean plan [--config PATH] [--policy-namespace NS] [--scope …] [--fail-on-blocked] [-o json|yaml]
xp-clean trace --name ns/name|--name name -n ns --group G --kind K [--version V] [-o text|json|yaml]
xp-clean manager [--config PATH] [--policy-namespace NS]
xp-clean version [-o short|json|yaml]
xp-clean completion bash|zsh|fish|powershell
Command Role run --once Discover → plan → optional execute (CronJob-friendly) plan Planner output only (always dry-run semantics for deletes) trace Print one composition tree manager Long-running schedule stub version / completion Build metadata and shell completion

docs.title: Flags worth knowing
docs.text:
Flag / env Notes --config / XP_CLEAN_CONFIG Required for file override — no implicit sample path --policy-namespace / XP_CLEAN_POLICY_NAMESPACE Namespace for labelled ConfigMaps (default xp-clean) --dry-run / XP_CLEAN_DRY_RUN Boolean planner dry-run (not kubectl API-server dry-run). Unset keeps policy value (default true) --scope / XP_CLEAN_SCOPE instances-only (default) or all --fail-on-blocked Exit 3 when the run completed with blocked plans --notify / XP_CLEAN_NOTIFY Override notifications.enabled --notify-on-dry-run / XP_CLEAN_NOTIFY_ON_DRY_RUN Override notifications.onDryRun -n / --namespace Valid on trace only. Rejected on run / plan (usage / exit 2)

Logging uses zap/logr on stderr (--zap-devel, --zap-log-level, --zap-encoder). Machine output (plan, trace -o json|yaml, audit JSON on run) stays on stdout.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Success 1 Runtime failure 2 Usage / validation (including -n on run/plan) 3 Blocked plans with --fail-on-blocked

docs.title: Precedence
docs.text: Flags > env > policy document > built-in defaults. No Viper. Webhook URLs come only from env vars named by each sink (default XP_CLEAN_TEAMS_WEBHOOK_URL).

docs.title: ConfigMap policy
docs.text: In-cluster policy configuration uses ConfigMaps in the dedicated xp-clean namespace. A future CleanupPolicy CRD may add richer status UX — ConfigMaps remain the primary surface and are not demoted.

docs.title: Discovery rules
docs.text:
Requirement Value Namespace Dedicated xp-clean by default (--policy-namespace / XP_CLEAN_POLICY_NAMESPACE) Label xp-clean.io/policy=true Data key policy.yaml

Multiple labelled ConfigMaps may coexist for per-team multi-tenancy (different TTLs / globs per team).

Samples in the repository:

  • config/samples/configmap.yaml — team A
  • config/samples/configmap-team-b.yaml — team B
  • config/samples/cleanuppolicy.yaml — file form for --config only

docs.title: File override
docs.text: Pass --config PATH (or XP_CLEAN_CONFIG) for local or mounted file use. There is no implicit repo-relative sample path.

docs.title: Policy document shape (summary)
docs.text:
name: team-a
schedule: "0 */6 * * *"
dryRun: true
timezone: Europe/London
selectors:
  requireLabels:
    xp-clean.io/eligible: "true"
  globs:
    namespaces: ["team-a-*", "xp-test-*"]
    xrdNames: ["*.dev.example.org"]
    xrNames: ["test-*"]
    gvks: ["*.dev.example.org/*"]   # group/version; kind not required
  namespaceDeny: ["kube-system", "crossplane-system"]
ttl:
  respectResourceTTL: true
  defaultTTL: 168h
  applyDefaultTTLIfMissing: false
deletion:
  scope: instances-only             # or all
  maxTracesPerRun: 20
  maxDeletesPerRun: 100
  orphanMode: report
  deletePaused: false
  allowXRDDeletion: false
  waitTimeout: 30m
observability:
  verbosity: normal
  notifications:
    enabled: false
    # … see Notifications

Audit events go to stdout JSON only for now — no audit ConfigMap or object-storage retention sink.

docs.title: RBAC note
docs.text: Lab / backend installs may use broad reader/deleter ClusterRoles for now; tighten later. Prefer installing into the dedicated xp-clean namespace (Helm default when the chart lands).

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• British English in user-facing docs.
  • Prefer ConfigMap / file policy samples that match locked product decisions (eligibility labels/globs, instances-only default, Teams notify schema, no claim support).

docs.title: Eligibility
docs.text:
Matching uses labels and/or glob patterns. Operators may use labels, globs, or both. When both are set, an object must satisfy all non-empty constraint groups (AND).

Mechanism Examples Labels requireLabels: { xp-clean.io/eligible: "true" } Namespace globs team-*-dev, xp-test-* XRD / XR name globs *.dev.example.org, test-* GVK globs group/version patterns (kind not required), e.g. *.dev.example.org/* Deny list namespaceDeny: [kube-system, crossplane-system]

Namespace alone is not enough

Namespace-implies-eligibility is not the model. Eligibility never comes from -n / --namespace on run or plan (that flag is rejected there). Use policy labels and/or globs only.

TTL fields (respectResourceTTL, defaultTTL, …) gate when an eligible stack is old enough to delete.

docs.title: Deletion scope
docs.text: deletion.scope Behaviour instances-only (default) Safer — XRs and composed resources / MRs all Instances first, then definitions (CompositionRevision → Composition → XRD) that have zero remaining instances and match selectors. XRD also needs allowXRDDeletion: true

docs.title: Safety gates
docs.text:
• Dry-run by default — planner dry-run; live deletes need policy dryRun: false and --dry-run=false.
  • Paused resources — skipped by default (crossplane.io/paused) unless deletePaused: true.
  • Keep label — xp-clean.io/keep=true skips the whole trace.
  • Budgets — maxTracesPerRun / maxDeletesPerRun.
  • Finalizers — Xp-clean never strips Crossplane finalizers; cloud objects are deleted by Crossplane’s own controllers.
  • Claims / LegacyCluster — out of scope; XR-only / v2-native path.
  • Orphans — orphanMode: report (MVP) surfaces orphans without inventing parallel ownership.

docs.title: Run flow (summary)
docs.text:
discover XRDs / XRs
  → match labels/globs + TTL
  → build traces (parent→child)
  → plan deletions (scope + gates)
  → execute (unless dry-run)
  → audit JSON on stdout (+ optional Teams notify)

docs.title: Install and releases
docs.text: Tagged SemVer releases (v*) publish release artefacts. There is no snapshot publish from main.

docs.title: Artefacts
docs.text:
1. GitHub Release archives — linux and darwin (amd64 / arm64) plus checksums.txt (and archive SBOMs when Syft is available on the runner).
  2. Private GHCR image — ghcr.io/kanzifucius/xp-clean (linux amd64 / arm64).
Image tag Meaning :vX.Y.Z Immutable pin (prefer this in clusters) :X.Y / :X Floating minor / major on non-prerelease cuts :latest Moved only on non-prerelease releases (RCs such as v0.2.0-rc.1 do not move it)

GHCR packages stay private (match the private repository).

docs.title: Pull a private image
docs.text:
# PAT or fine-grained token with read:packages (SSO-authorise if the org requires it)
echo "$CR_PAT" | docker login ghcr.io -u USERNAME --password-stdin
docker pull ghcr.io/kanzifucius/xp-clean:v0.1.0

In-cluster pulls need an imagePullSecret whose token can read:packages for ghcr.io/kanzifucius/xp-clean.

docs.title: Cut a release (maintainers)
docs.text:
1. Ensure main is green.
  2. Tag and push (do not create the Release in the UI):
git checkout main && git pull
git tag -a v0.1.0 -m "v0.1.0"
git push origin v0.1.0
  1. Watch the release workflow; confirm GitHub Release assets and docker pull ghcr.io/kanzifucius/xp-clean:v0.1.0.
  2. Spot-check xp-clean version -o json from the archive or image.

The docs workflow also deploys a versioned site for that tag (see Home for latest / dev aliases).

Release notes and assets: GitHub Releases.

docs.text: SPDX / licence packaging for OCI labels is deferred for now — revisit when the repository adds an explicit LICENSE.

docs.title: Notifications (Teams)
docs.text:
Chat summaries sit beside stdout audit JSON and metrics. They wrap each RunOnce (started / finished / failed), use a short HTTP deadline, and never change cleanup results or exit codes.

MVP sink: Microsoft Teams Workflows. Slack shares the multi-sink schema but is not implemented yet.

docs.title: Decisions (locked)
docs.text:
• Notify on run start when notifications are enabled (started in notifyOn).
  • Multi-sink schema from day one; Teams first.
  • onDryRun: true — dry-run runs still notify when enabled.
  • Optional logURLTemplate for log deep-links ({{runId}} substituted).
  • SSRF host allow-list is guidance-only for MVP (https-only client; no redirect following).
  • Ships with ConfigMap / --config now — do not wait for a CleanupPolicy CRD.

docs.title: Teams Workflow setup
docs.text:
1. In Teams, create a Workflow owned by the platform team or a channel owner (both are valid; prefer co-owners).
  2. Trigger: When a Teams webhook request is received.
  3. Action: Post card in a chat or channel.
  4. Copy the Workflow callback URL into a Kubernetes Secret (or local env) as XP_CLEAN_TEAMS_WEBHOOK_URL.
  5. Never commit the URL to git or put it in the ConfigMap policy body.

docs.title: Policy snippet
docs.text:
observability:
  notifications:
    enabled: true
    notifyOn: [started, finished, failed]
    onDryRun: true
    sinks:
      - type: teams
        webhookURLFromEnv: XP_CLEAN_TEAMS_WEBHOOK_URL
        logURLTemplate: "https://logs.example/search?q={{runId}}"  # optional

Mount the Secret as an env var on the Job / CronJob / Deployment. Overrides:

Flag / env Effect --notify / XP_CLEAN_NOTIFY Override notifications.enabled --notify-on-dry-run / XP_CLEAN_NOTIFY_ON_DRY_RUN Override onDryRun

docs.title: Failure isolation
docs.text: Notify failures are logged and ignored for exit codes. Missing webhook config is a noop. Partial multi-sink failure does not fail cleanup. Audit JSON remains authoritative for what was deleted.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: Build a local binary, point at a sample policy with an explicit --config, and run a dry-run plan against a cluster that can list XRDs.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Go matching go.mod (see repository root)
  • A kubeconfig that can list XRDs and the XR GVKs your selectors match

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
make test
make build   # writes bin/xp-clean with version ldflags

docs.title: Dry-run locally (file override)
docs.text:
There is no implicit sample path. Pass --config every time you use a file:

go run ./cmd/xp-clean run --once \
  --config config/samples/cleanuppolicy.yaml \
  --dry-run=true \
  --kubeconfig "$HOME/.kube/config"

Inspect the planner output without executing:

go run ./cmd/xp-clean plan --config config/samples/cleanuppolicy.yaml -o json

Trace one XR:

go run ./cmd/xp-clean trace \
  --name test-db -n xp-test-1 \
  --group db.dev.example.org \
  --kind XDB

Live deletes

Live deletes require dryRun: false in the policy and --dry-run=false. Prefer dry-run until the plan looks correct. Xp-clean never strips Crossplane finalizers.

docs.title: In-cluster sketch
docs.text:
1. Create the dedicated xp-clean namespace.
  2. Deploy a ServiceAccount + RBAC — see config/rbac/role.yaml in the repository.
  3. Apply one or more labelled policy ConfigMaps (label xp-clean.io/policy=true, data key policy.yaml). Samples: configmap.yaml, configmap-team-b.yaml.
  4. Run either:
    • Job / CronJob: xp-clean run --once (loads ConfigMaps; optional --config override)
    • Deployment: xp-clean manager (interval stub; controller-runtime later)

See ConfigMap policy and Install and releases for GHCR pull and release notes.
